cse-2015-3-cs-36.approach: Draw the timeline packet by packet: two 5000-bit packets, store-and-forward with a 35 µs processing delay at the switch. The answer is the moment the last bit of packet 2 reaches the receiver.
cse-2015-3-cs-36.given:
| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Link rate | $10^7$ bps |
| Propagation per link | 20 µs |
| Switch processing | 35 µs |
| Data / packet size | 10000 / 5000 bits → 2 packets |

steps.title: Per-packet transmission time
steps.body:
$$T_t=\frac{5000}{10^7}\text{ s}=5\times10^{-4}\text{ s}=500\ \mu s$$
The source sends P1 during $[0,500]$ and P2 during $[500,1000]$.

scene.caption: Source transmits both packets back to back.

steps.title: Packet 1 through the switch
steps.body: Last bit of P1 reaches the switch at $500+20=520$. Forwarding starts at $520+35=555$ and ends at $555+500=1055$; the last bit reaches the receiver at $1055+20=1075$.

steps.title: Packet 2 through the switch
steps.body:
Last bit of P2 reaches the switch at $1000+20=1020$; it is ready at $1020+35=1055$, exactly when the outgoing link becomes free (P1 finished at 1055), so there is no queueing. Transmission $1055\to1555$, then propagation:
$$1555+20=1575\ \mu s$$

cse-2015-3-cs-36.shortcut: First packet end to end: $500+20+35+500+20=1075$; every further packet adds one $T_t$ (the links are the bottleneck): $1075+500=1575$.
pitfalls: Sending all 10000 bits as one packet (that gives $1000+20+35+1000+20=2075$).
Adding the 35 µs switch delay only once for both packets incorrectly or forgetting it.

cse-2015-3-cs-37.approach: Condition on $X_3=0$: XOR with 0 changes nothing, so $Y=X_1X_2$, and since $X_3$ is independent of $X_1,X_2$ the condition can be dropped.

steps.title: Simplify Y under the condition
steps.body: With $X_3=0$: $Y=X_1X_2\oplus0=X_1X_2$.

steps.title: Compute the probability
steps.body:
$X_1X_2=1$ only when both are 1: $\Pr=\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac12=\tfrac14$. As $X_1,X_2$ are independent of $X_3$,
$$\Pr[Y=0\mid X_3=0]=1-\tfrac14=\tfrac34=0.75$$

cse-2015-3-cs-37.verification: Enumerated $(X_1,X_2)\in\{00,01,10,11\}$: products $0,0,0,1$, so 3 of the 4 equally likely cases give $Y=0$.

cse-2015-3-cs-38.approach: A /27 mask leaves 5 host bits, so subnets are blocks of 32 in the last octet. AND 144 with the mask to find the real block, then the last host is broadcast − 1.

steps.title: Mask the last octet
steps.body:
Host bits $=32-27=5$, so the mask's last octet is $11100000_2=224$.
$$144=10010000_2,\quad 10010000_2\wedge11100000_2=10000000_2=128$$
So 200.10.11.144 lies in the /27 block that starts at **.128** (144 is not a multiple of 32).

steps.title: Broadcast and last host
steps.body:
Block $=128\ldots128+31=159$. Broadcast $=200.10.11.159$, so the last assignable host is $200.10.11.158$.

Fourth octet $=\mathbf{158}$.

pitfalls: Treating .144 as the network address and counting 144 + 31 = 175 → 174; a /27 network address must be a multiple of 32 in the last octet.
cse-2015-3-cs-38.verification: Blocks of 32: 0, 32, 64, 96, 128, 160 — 144 falls in 128–159, so the answer 158 is the official GATE key.

steps.title: Reflexive?
steps.body: $((p,q),(p,q))\in R$ needs $p-q=q-p$, i.e. $p=q$. For $(1,2)$: $1-2=-1\ne1=2-1$. **Not reflexive.**

cse-2015-3-cs-45.approach: Replace $x$ by $1/x$ to get a second equation, solve the 2×2 linear system for $f(x)$, then integrate from 1 to 2.

steps.title: Second equation
steps.body: Substituting $x\to1/x$: $af(1/x)+bf(x)=x-25$.

steps.title: Solve for f(x)
steps.body:
Multiply the original by $a$ and the new one by $b$ and subtract:
$$(a^2-b^2)f(x)=a\left(\tfrac1x-25\right)-b(x-25)=\tfrac ax-25a-bx+25b$$

steps.title: Integrate
steps.body:
$$\int_1^2\left(\tfrac ax-25a-bx+25b\right)dx=a\ln2-25a-b\cdot\tfrac{4-1}{2}+25b=a(\ln2-25)+b\left(25-\tfrac32\right)=a(\ln2-25)+\tfrac{47b}{2}$$
So $\int_1^2f(x)\,dx=\frac{1}{a^2-b^2}\left[a(\ln2-25)+\frac{47b}{2}\right]$.

optionAnalysis.reason: Matches the derivation.
Wrong coefficient of $\ln2$ and wrong sign of the $b$ term.
$\int_1^2\frac1x\,dx=\ln2$, not $2\ln2$.
The $b$ term is $+25b-\tfrac32b=+\tfrac{47b}{2}$, not negative.
